extracted.intended_audience: organizations and potential grantees seeking funding from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the Gates Foundation's funding policies, eligibility rules, priorities, and procedural expectations for organizations and partners seeking grants or strategic investments. Covers what is funded, what is not, decision criteria, and grantee expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding mechanisms: committed grants and strategic investments
rubrics_metrics.description: We primarily invest in two ways: committed grants and strategic investments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committed grants account for the majority of charitable giving to organizations. Strategic investments "bring the resources and expertise of the private sector to issues that would otherwise not be addressed due to market failures." Use grants for mission-aligned programmatic work; use strategic investments where private-sector capital/expertise can address market failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantee type: organizations (not individuals, with rare exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide grants ... to organizations to achieve measurable impact in the fight against poverty, disease, and inequity around the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation generally does not make grants directly to individuals except in specific, rare circumstances or within programs designed to accept applications from individual researchers and innovators (e.g., certain Grand Challenges initiatives and other requests for proposal). Most funding is therefore intended for organizational recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive grantmaking: unsolicited proposals generally not accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of our grantmaking and strategic investing is proactive—that is, we identify organizations that might be well-suited to carrying out a project we initiate, and we directly invite them to submit a funding proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation states it "generally do[es] not accept unsolicited proposals." Potential applicants should look for specific 'Open grant opportunities' or invitations rather than expecting to submit unsolicited requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global access requirements for funded work and products
rubrics_metrics.description: All of our charitable funding to organizations—including private sector organizations—comes with global access requirements to ensure that the knowledge gained through the funding is shared publicly and that products funded by us are made available and accessible at an affordable price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should expect conditions requiring open sharing of research outputs and ensuring affordability/availability of products developed with Foundation funds. This applies also to for-profit partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and open access expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: We aim to be as transparent as possible about our work, including by reporting to third-party transparency initiatives and making all foundation-funded research openly accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation publishes searchable lists of grantees and investment partners and provides financial reports and annual reports. Funded research is expected to be made openly accessible; applicants should plan for public sharing and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and regulatory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: We abide by all laws governing U.S.-based private foundations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and partners should be prepared to comply with legal and regulatory requirements applicable to U.S. private foundations and any contractual terms the Foundation requires.

rubrics_metrics.name: What we do not fund (excluded categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not provide funding for: Political campaigns or direct lobbying efforts; Building or capital campaigns; Projects with an exclusively religious purpose; Projects that address health issues in high-income countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are explicit exclusions. Proposals involving political activities, direct lobbying, capital fundraising for buildings, exclusively religious purposes, or health work targeted only at high-income countries will generally be ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority decision criteria: comparative advantage and potential to reduce inequity
rubrics_metrics.description: We start by identifying where we have a comparative advantage and where our engagement can unlock a reduction in inequity. We prioritize areas where the inequity is large—and so is the potential for reducing it with catalytic interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate how the Foundation's involvement would be strategic (comparative advantage), and show potential for catalytic, measurable reductions in inequity. Priority is given to areas with large inequities and high potential impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of philanthropic capital: fill gaps left by public and private capital
rubrics_metrics.description: Private capital naturally flows to the most profitable opportunities. Public capital (i.e., government spending) naturally flows to lower-risk opportunities. One role of philanthropic capital can be to fill the gaps created by public and private capital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should articulate how proposed work addresses gaps not adequately served by private or public funding—e.g., higher-risk, high-need, or less profitable interventions where philanthropy can catalyze change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner selection criteria: technical expertise, diverse perspectives, and local presence
rubrics_metrics.description: We are committed to building a network of grantees and partners with unparalleled technical expertise and diverse perspectives. We are increasingly working with a broader array of partners, especially those headquartered in the geographies where the work is taking place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred partners demonstrate strong technical capacity, a diversity of perspectives, and local leadership/headquarters in the regions where work will be implemented. Collaboration and partnerships that broaden expertise are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic investments target market failures
rubrics_metrics.description: We also make strategic investments that bring the resources and expertise of the private sector to issues that would otherwise not be addressed due to market failures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic investment proposals should show how private-sector mechanisms and capital can address market failures and create sustainable solutions where grants alone may not suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure of grantees and program topics
rubrics_metrics.description: We make public a searchable list of our past and present grantees and strategic investment partners, along with the project topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can review published grantee lists and project topics to understand portfolio priorities and past/ongoing work. Expect public disclosure of awarded projects and topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantee relations: respect and candor
rubrics_metrics.description: Our grantees and partners are at the core of our mission and work. We are committed to treating them with respect and communicating with candor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation sets an expectation for professional, respectful, and candid communications with grantees; applicants should anticipate direct, transparent engagement if funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial transparency and reporting (annual reports & audited documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: We are committed to providing clear, timely information on our finances and grantmaking efforts. View our annual reports from 1998 to 2024. View our audited financial documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation maintains published annual reports and audited financials; grantees and partners should be prepared for financial reporting requirements and public financial transparency related to grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to find opportunities: consult Grant Opportunities and Open RFPs
rubrics_metrics.description: Is my organization eligible to receive funding through the foundation? See our Grant Opportunities. We make certain programs and RFPs available that accept applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because most funding is proactive, potential applicants should monitor the Foundation's 'Grant Opportunities' and 'Open grant opportunities' pages for eligibility details and application pathways (including occasional RFPs and Grand Challenges that accept individual applicants).
